summary: Learn data quality engineering with Great Expectations, dbt tests, and monitoring dashboards. Build practical controls and improve data trust.
lede: Data quality engineering and monitoring helps you turn scattered checks into a structured way to protect data across ingestion, transformation, and delivery. You will learn to profile datasets, map business rules to test cases, automate validation, monitor freshness and schema drift, and track defects against clear quality thresholds. Using the six data quality dimensions, Great Expectations, dbt tests, and data observability patterns, the course develops practical skills in alerting, issue logging, dashboard configuration, and remediation workflows. You will apply these methods to realistic warehouse and analytics scenarios while managing incomplete metadata, legacy ETL logic, competing deadlines, and inconsistent ownership, then communicate quality trends clearly to technical and business stakeholders.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to design, monitor, and govern trusted data pipelines in real operational settings. It speaks to the people who own validation rules, fix recurring defects, and report data quality status to business and technology leaders.
prerequisites: Prerequisites required: working knowledge of SQL, basic data warehouse concepts, and familiarity with data pipelines or ETL workflows. You should be comfortable reading table structures, simple transformation logic, and business rules. No programming is required for completion, although prior exposure to dbt, Python, or data observability tools will help you move faster. Advanced concepts are taught at an operational application level, with tool-based exercises focused on monitoring design, validation logic, and issue triage rather than production engineering.
